text: Euroleague's president Bodiroga "Expansion and the introduction of franchises are coming. Starting next season, we will move from the current 20-team format, in which every team plays every other team, to 24 teams, with what will essentially be 2 conferences". NBA Europe wasn't mentioned. Serbian outlet Mozzart Sport has reported Dejan Bodiroga’s latest comments on the present and future of the EuroLeague, made to Radar Forum. “The EuroLeague has never been stronger than it is today. We are growing and progressing according to plan,” the EuroLeague Basketball president said. “I’ll give you a brief overview of the competition’s current situation, focusing on a few key figures. Last year, more than 3.3 million fans attended our games, while over 500 million people watched them on television throughout the season. That’s an all-time high. “We have also seen significant growth and reached new records on social media. The number of sponsors, partners and fans is increasing as well. All the numbers show that the EuroLeague is in a positive position. That was one of the reasons we met in Italy last week to discuss the competition’s future. It was a positive and important meeting, where we discussed the next steps.” “Expansion and the introduction of franchises are on the agenda. Starting next season, we will move from the current 20-team format, in which every team plays every other team, to 24 teams, with what will essentially be two conferences. We have not yet determined the criteria for forming them. “Franchises are also coming. We have received numerous expressions of interest and several offers, both from EuroCup teams and from clubs outside the competition. They have submitted binding offers, expressing their desire to become EuroLeague members in the future. “Crvena Zvezda and Partizan are naturally among them. I believe both clubs are held in high regard by our board. Given the process, their involvement and the requirements they need to meet, I think they have a very good chance of joining the EuroLeague. Simply put, I see them as long-term partners of the competition.” As for NBA Europe, there was nothing new to report. Source: [https://sportando.basketball/en/euroleague-bodiroga-starting-next-season-well-have-24-teams-and-two-conferences/](https://sportando.basketball/en/euroleague-bodiroga-starting-next-season-well-have-24-teams-and-two-conferences/)

text: In his new ESPN documentary, Ben Simmons called out Doc Rivers' reaction after the infamous G7 vs Atlanta "How did I feel? I was like 'What a piece of s**t'. He didn't want to lose his job. When times get tough people start panicking and throwing others under the bus. That's it's just what happened" One of the main subjects the documentary explores is Philadelphia's heartbreaking loss to the Atlanta Hawks in Game 7 of the 2021 Eastern Conference semifinals. Simmons faced intense criticism after passing the ball instead of attempting an open dunk late in the game. The moment quickly became one of the most discussed plays of his career and intensified the pressure surrounding the young star. "How did I feel? I was like, 'What a piece of 'shit,'" Simmons said in the documentary about his head coach at the time, Doc Rivers. Simmons added: "When you have a relationship with somebody, and they have your back, I think certain things are supposed to be handled certain ways. But then you also gotta look at it from the side of 'he's got a job.' You know, he's making his money." "He ain't trying to lose his job or anything like that. So, when times get tough, people start panicking. People throw people under the bus, and that's just, it's just what happened." Source: [https://basketnews.com/news-257527-ben-simmons-used-an-expletive-to-describe-doc-rivers-in-his-new-documentary.html](https://basketnews.com/news-257527-ben-simmons-used-an-expletive-to-describe-doc-rivers-in-his-new-documentary.html)

text: Before the season, LeBron James said he envisioned joining the Knicks as free agent if they didn't win the title. Would the Knicks have tinkered with their roster to accommodate that? A few weeks ago, LeBron confirmed this and said that the potential backlash from joining the Knicks after they had won the title rescinded that idea. Source: http://espn.com/nba/story/_/id/50053106/lebron-james-says-envisioned-joining-knicks-free-agent One route would have been a trade of KAT for LeBron since their salaries were close enough to make this a 1-1 trade (assuming LeBron opted in), and it could have kept Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart together. Other versions of a trade would have sent out multiple players and picks, costing the Knicks depth and a step back from a roster that was already a title contender (highly unlikely the Knicks would have accommodated that). Other than that, LeBron could have signed for the vet minimum, forcing one of their guys to the bench (likely Hart, who wouldn't be too happy as he's expiring also). Would the Knicks have entertained gutting their roster a little bit and messing with chemistry to accommodate signing a 41 year old LeBron?
